speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the onset and severity of your right flank pain, and have you noticed any blood in your urine?

text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any fever or chills, and does the pain radiate toward your groin or lower abdomen? Have you noticed any changes in your urinary frequency or urgency?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience nausea or vomiting along with the pain, and does the discomfort feel like it comes in waves? Have you noticed any decrease in urine output or swelling in your legs?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history except noted recurrent urinary tract infections. No history of renal dialysis or known genetic diseases. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works in an office setting.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of kidney stones, and have you noticed any difficulty passing urine or a change in the stream? I would like to see imaging to evaluate the urinary tract. REQUEST IMAGES

text: Denies fever, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dysuria, or any recent illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of recurrent UTIs and current hematuria, I need to rule out structural abnormalities or chronic infection. REQUEST TEST: Urine_Culture_and_Sensitivity, Ultrasound_Kidney

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the initial imaging and urine culture are normal, I need to rule out malignancy or upper tract pathology. REQUEST TEST: CT_Urography, Cystoscopy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT_Urography: No renal masses, stones, or hydronephrosis identified. Normal excretion of contrast. Cystoscopy: No bladder masses, tumors, or signs of interstitial cystitis. Normal bladder mucosa.

text: Given the negative imaging and cystoscopy, I need to assess for glomerular disease. Do you have any history of high blood pressure, diabetes, or joint pain, and have you noticed any foamy urine or swelling in your ankles?
